title: The model is numerate. The headline is where it gets weird.
dek: Why this site keeps the numbers, the caveats, and the occasional joke in three different drawers.
author: The Quant's interpreter
original_contribution: A public operating note explaining how sourced market records become a finite plain-English edition without dropping their boundaries.
limitations: This is an editorial operating note, not a market finding or investment advice.

sections.heading: One finite edition, two jobs
paragraphs: A source record says what changed. The translation explains why a general reader might care without turning that record into personal advice or a transaction recommendation.
The original page stays canonical, because attribution is not a decorative footnote and search engines should not have to guess which copy is real.

sections.heading: The joke stops before the evidence starts
paragraphs: The wrapper can be funny. A limitation cannot. Dates, evidence classes, missing coverage and countercases travel with the story even when the headline has better timing than the model.
If a feed goes missing, the page says coverage gap. It does not translate silence into calm, confidence, or a convenient advertisement.

sections.heading: Advertising gets its own box
paragraphs: Sponsors can buy clearly labelled space around the reporting. They cannot buy a finding, a product ranking, or a quieter limitation. The separation is both an editorial rule and a useful way to avoid making every paragraph sound like a pitch deck.
